verdict: No runtime blocker found in the frozen live instructions; one optional wording improvement. Recorded runtime supports the three-maker fallback, with the stated coverage limits.

optional_suggestions.finding: Later default-five wording could use the requested role count consistently. In particular parallel-production.md:11 says to preserve five roles/five final images after line 3 already establishes a user quantity override. Several SKILL passages and the default_prompt likewise use five as shorthand.
optional_suggestions.why_not_blocker: SKILL.md:10,17,20 and parallel-production.md:3 explicitly give the user count precedence, and the one-image maker contract prevents expansion. The runtime can follow these instructions without changing the requested count.
optional_suggestions.suggestion: At the concurrency fallback sentence, say to preserve the requested role/image total, with five identified as the default. This is a clarity change, not a new production rule.

no_change_passes.finding: The coordinator must assign five distinct one-image maker agents by default; all five run simultaneously if maker capacity permits. Lower capacity runs the supported number and queues remaining roles without creating other chats to bypass limits.
Explicit quantity overrides the default, aspect ratios are allocated within that total, and a one-image follow-up changes only the named image and requested part. Count ownership is central.

The coordinator owns exact copy, common constraints and distinct organizing relationships. Makers own concrete composition within their assigned one-image direction and report changes. Maker mode forbids recursive maker spawning.

no_change_passes.topic: Peer output isolation and actual references
no_change_passes.finding: Makers cannot read or reuse peer images/prompts; new calls do not automatically inherit earlier directions. Real user references are preserved and their role is specified using the current tool schema.

Exact spelling, spacing, numeric values, names, punctuation and fixed line breaks are retained. The new dense-copy editing guidance also preserves user-specified order. Explicit neon, chrome, 3D and other styles remain mandatory.

Instructions require a real built-in image call and current supported arguments. A maximum-resolution prompt is explicitly distinguished from actual output control or proof; returned dimensions must be checked and upscaling is not original detail.

Regeneration counts toward two automatic corrections per image. Coordinator and maker calls are combined; duplicate concurrent repair is prohibited and failed roles continue only within the remaining budget. Evaluation retains ordinary limits.

no_change_passes.topic: Content direction comparison without templates or bans
no_change_passes.finding: The changed comparison checks content identification, usable copy, organization and the nearest direction before dispatch. It accepts direct photographs, quiet titles, familiar type and a shared reading order when other spatial/editorial relationships differ. No color, effect, photograph, print style or font automatically passes or fails. Maker layouts are not centrally cloned.

The permitted case file explicitly declares a new user-requested phase, 14 initial outputs, at most two automatic repairs per new output, a 42-call phase cap and a 76-call combined cap including 34 historical calls. This is disclosed additional evaluation, not a silent extension of the historical budget.

All six relative Markdown links in the live skill package resolve. UI metadata uses the correct skill token and is consistent with default production; metadata and evaluation-loop.md are unchanged against main.

runtime_evidence.status: Recorded aggregate evidence only; raw call timing not independently audited.

checks.standard_validator: Unavailable: ModuleNotFoundError: yaml in shell and bundled Python

git_diff_main.scope: Content relationship comparison, maker autonomy within assigned direction, dense-copy editing, and additional research references.

limitations: The execution roster records 14 distinct makers, five distinct makers for the default case, three supported simultaneous makers, three actual concurrent makers, and three overlapping recorded native-call intervals. These aggregates support fallback execution. Raw timing/call logs were outside this audit and were not independently reconstructed.

The permitted cases cover default five outputs, explicit two-output cases and one new single-image case. They contain no one-image follow-up edit. That behavior passes instruction review but is not runtime-verified here. A five-simultaneous execution is also untested because the recorded environment supports three makers.

The standard skill-creator quick_validate.py was attempted with shell Python and bundled Python. Both stopped before validation because PyYAML is unavailable. No packages were installed. Local link existence and the simple frontmatter/metadata structure were checked directly; these do not replace the unavailable validator.

No images, blind packets/mappings, image review reports, production prompts, manifests, call ledger or visual-quality evidence were opened. This audit makes no claim about generated-image quality or native tool-call argument compliance in recorded productions.
